entities.summary: Otto Robert Frisch was an Austrian-born British physicist who worked on nuclear physics. With Otto Stern and Immanuel Estermann, he first measured the magnetic moment of the proton. With his aunt, Lise Meitner, he advanced the first theoretical explanation of nuclear fission and first experimentally detected the fission by-products. Later, with his collaborator, Rudolf Peierls, he designed the first theoretical mechanism for the detonation of an atomic bomb in 1940. Leading the Los Alamos Critical Assemblies experiments in 1945, he oversaw the world's first prompt criticality in the Dragon device.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Frisch's work on nuclear fission led to the development of atomic bombs during World War II, with his design contributing to the detonation of the first atomic bomb in 1945. His research also advanced our understanding of nuclear physics and its applications.
